# 002 — Xcode project generated by XcodeGen, not committed

**Status:** accepted · 2026-10-18

## Context

The app has 5 targets (app, 3 Screen Time extensions, unit tests), each with its own bundle ID, entitlements and `Info.plist`, plus shared sources compiled into four of them. Xcode stores all of this in `project.pbxproj`, a file of random-looking IDs that is hard to review in a pull request and conflicts badly when two branches add files.

## Decision

- `ios/project.yml` is the source of truth. `xcodegen generate` produces `ios/QuestLock.xcodeproj`.
- The generated `.xcodeproj` is **gitignored**. CI and every fresh clone run `xcodegen generate` first.
- Entitlements and extension `Info.plist` keys live in `project.yml` (`entitlements.properties` and `info.properties`). XcodeGen rewrites the `.entitlements`/`Info.plist` files on every run, so hand edits to them are lost.
- Signing team comes from the gitignored `ios/Config/Debug.xcconfig` (template: `Debug.xcconfig.example`), so the public repo builds for anyone and CI builds unsigned.

## Alternatives considered

- **Commit the `.xcodeproj` and edit it in Xcode**: the default, but every target or capability change becomes an unreadable `.pbxproj` diff.
- **Commit both `project.yml` and the generated project**: diffs stay readable, but the two can drift and there is nothing to gain from it.
- **Tuist**: more powerful (Swift manifests, caching), but heavier and a new dependency to learn. More than a 5-target app needs.
